title: AML Compliance Review: Transaction Monitoring Effectiveness, Customer Due Diligence Quality, Suspicious Activity Reporting Statistics, and Recommended Programme Enhancements
subtitle: AML Compliance Review | Transaction Monitoring, Customer Due Diligence, SAR Metrics & Programme Enhancements

document_brief.narrative_theme: This AML compliance review demonstrates how targeted improvements to transaction monitoring, customer due diligence, and SAR operations can measurably reduce alert backlogs, improve investigative quality, and strengthen regulatory readiness across 2024–2025.

sections.heading: Transaction Monitoring Effectiveness and Alert-to-Case Conversion (Q1 2024–Q1 2025)
key_facts: In Q1 2025, the transaction monitoring system generated 48,620 alerts, up from 41,880 in Q4 2024.
The alert-to-case conversion rate decreased from 7.8% in Q4 2024 to 6.1% in Q1 2025.
The median alert clearance time increased to 3.6 days in March 2025 from 2.4 days in December 2024.

sections.heading: Customer Due Diligence Quality, Suspicious Activity Reporting Performance, and Programme Enhancements (2024 Results)
key_facts: A CDD QA review of 300 files completed on 15 February 2025 found an 18.0% material deficiency rate (54 of 300).
In 2024, 1,246 SARs were filed, and 312 SARs were filed within 30 days of initial detection (25.0%).
The recommended programme roadmap targets reducing the material CDD deficiency rate to 10.0% by 30 September 2025.

structure.heading: Customer Due Diligence Quality, Suspicious Activity Reporting Performance, and Programme Enhancements (2024 Results)
text_content: **Customer Due Diligence Quality, Suspicious Activity Reporting Performance, and Programme Enhancements (2024 Results)**

On 15 February 2025, the Compliance Quality Assurance team completed a CDD QA review of 300 account files and identified a material deficiency rate of 18.0% (54 of 300). The deficiencies were concentrated in outdated source-of-funds documentation, inadequate risk-scoring rationale, and incomplete beneficial ownership verification for legal-entity customers. Findings indicate systemic weaknesses in front-line collection and first-line supervisory sign-off. Remediation priorities include immediate file cures for 54 identified accounts, additional targeted re-training for 150 onboarding officers, and a six-week retrospective review of new client acceptances from Q4 2024 to identify gaps. The CDD QA report was presented to Compliance Leadership on 20 February 2025.

In 2024 the Financial Crimes Reporting unit filed 1,246 suspicious activity reports (SARs), of which 312 were submitted within 30 days of initial detection, representing 25.0% timeliness. The remaining 75.0% were subject to extended investigation timelines driven by complex cross-jurisdictional inquiries, additional evidence collection, and enhanced due diligence on higher-risk entities. Internal review identified case-management bottlenecks in evidence aggregation and legal review backlogs as primary contributors to delayed filings. Immediate corrective steps recommended include strengthening case triage, expanding the SAR investigation team by 12 full-time equivalents, and implementing a 30-day monitoring KPI with weekly senior-management dashboards to improve adherence to statutory expectations.

The recommended programme roadmap establishes clear milestones to reduce the material CDD deficiency rate from 18.0% to 10.0% by 30 September 2025. Key initiatives include: 1. policy refresh and standardized CDD checklists by 31 March 2025; 2. phased deployment of automated document verification and risk-scoring by 30 June 2025; 3. mandatory CDD certification for all relationship managers with quarterly assessments; and 4. monthly QA cycles with rolling sampling of 200 files and remediation SLAs. Progress will be tracked through a formal steering committee chaired by the Head of Compliance, with baseline (30 June 2025) and final assessments tied to executive remuneration metrics.

structure.heading: Transaction Monitoring Effectiveness and Alert-to-Case Conversion (Q1 2024–Q1 2025)
text_content: In Q1 2025 the transaction monitoring system generated 48,620 alerts, an increase from 41,880 alerts in Q4 2024. This 16.1% quarter-on-quarter rise strained analyst capacity and widened the review backlog across Retail Banking and Commercial lines. The higher volume corresponded with product launches and elevated cross-border flows in January and February 2025. Operationally, queue lengths and overtime hours rose; the average daily intake in March 2025 exceeded capacity planning assumptions that were calibrated to Q4 2024 volumes. The escalation in alerts necessitates immediate tuning and prioritisation to maintain risk coverage without unsustainable resource increases.

The alert-to-case conversion rate fell from 7.8% in Q4 2024 to 6.1% in Q1 2025, indicating lower yield per alert despite the higher volume. This decline suggests either an increase in false positives or that tuning thresholds are no longer aligned with evolving customer behaviour and risk typologies. Compliance and Line 1 partners should review rule-level performance and consider: 1. rebalancing threshold sensitivities; 2. retiring low-value alerts; and 3. implementing risk-scoring enhancements to prioritise high-probability examinations. A data-driven re-tuning plan with defined acceptance criteria is required by end of Q2 2025 to restore conversion performance.

The median alert clearance time increased to 3.6 days in March 2025 from 2.4 days in December 2024, reflecting backlog effects; remedial actions should include temporary analyst capacity, targeted automation for low-risk alerts, and tightened SLA monitoring through April–June 2025 immediately.
